title: Micro-emission accounting and KV-cache shadowing for per-token attribution
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: We need higher-fidelity attribution for per-token latency and cost that explicitly accounts for KV cache interactions and amortized batch effects. Current instrumentation aggregates at request-level and attributes cache savings as a coarse bucket; this hides regressions caused by suboptimal cache routing and prevents fine-grained billing/chargeback and regression alerts.

Goal: Build a micro-emission accounting layer that: 1) captures per-token timing slices (emit begin/end) with pointers to cache decision metadata; 2) records whether each token was served from KV cache, prefix cache, or full compute; 3) attributes per-token delta latency and estimated GPU compute cost after amortization for batching.

Design highlights:
- Tracing hooks: add two new span annotations at the emission pipeline: emission.slice.start and emission.slice.end. Each span carries attributes: token_index, token_hash, model_variant, batch_id, seq_len, kv_hit=true|false, kv_age_ms, routing_path. Spans should be lightweight (event-level) and sampled at 100% for first 24h in Canary, then 10% globally.
- KV-cache shadowing: introduce a "shadow decision" flag recorded when the routing layer consulted cache candidates (even if cache disabled) so we can measure missed-opportunity (shadow hits). This is required to estimate theoretical savings and to detect cache routing skew.
- Amortization windows: record batch_start_ts and batch_size on emission spans to allow later offline amortization of kernel setup / decode overhead across all tokens in a batch. This avoids overcharging single tokens for per-batch setup costs.
- Metrics/log pipeline: emit compact JSON lines to the local trace forwarder with keys required for downstream aggregation: ts, trace_id, emission_index, token_index, token_type (wordpiece|bpe), latency_ms, kv_status (hit|miss|shadow_hit), kv_age_ms, batch_id, model_name, model_version, instance_type. The trace forwarder will index these into ClickHouse with a partition by model_name and date.
- Dashboards and alerts: build a dedicated "token-economics" dashboard in Grafana with: per-token p50/p90/p99 by kv_status, distribution of kv_age for hits, shadow-hit rate by route, amortized cost per token by model, and a regression alert when amortized p95 latency increases by >15% vs baseline for two consecutive days.

Why this is different: we call out shadowing (measuring missed cache opportunities), explicit amortization metadata, and emit event-level spans designed to be inexpensive and compatible with existing tracing backends. This avoids reworking the whole tracing model and focuses on adding a small set of fields that unlock chargeback and regression detection.

Stakeholders: Runtime (Ethan Chen), Observability (Priya Gupta), Platform Data (Luca Romano), Product (Maya Singh).

Risks and mitigations:
- Volume: per-token events increase telemetry volume. Mitigate with sampling knobs and a compact event schema. Canary at 100% for limited traffic.
- Privacy: token_hash must be non-reversible. Use salted sha256 token fingerprint (no raw token text).
- Upstream storage/cost: ClickHouse schema must use low-cardinality tags where possible and TTLs. Coordinate with Platform Data for retention plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- emission.slice.start and emission.slice.end spans are emitted for all production emits in the canary cohort
- Each span contains token_index, token_hash (salted sha256), kv_status, kv_age_ms, batch_id, and model_version fields
- Shadow decision flag is emitted when routing evaluated cache candidates (even if not used)
- Forwarder stores compact JSON events into ClickHouse and test queries return per-token p50/p95 grouped by kv_status
- Grafana 'token-economics' dashboard shows amortized per-token cost charts and a working p95 regression alert
- Load tests show <8% additional network egress for canary and tailorable sampling reduces global overhead to <1% of current telemetry volume
implementation_notes:
Work split: 1) Runtime hooks (Ethan) — add span annotations and token-level timing helpers to emission path; 2) Routing/Cache (Priya) — emit shadow decision flag and kv metadata; 3) Forwarder/Schema (Luca) — add new compact JSON event type and ClickHouse table with appropriate indices and TTL; 4) Dashboards/Alerts (Maya/Product + Observability team) — design visualizations and create alert rules.

Important implementation details: use non-blocking emission of telemetry (batched to local forwarder). Use a 64-bit batch_id and monotonically increasing emission_index. Sampling control must be dynamic via flags in the config service to support ramp/canary. Add feature gate: token_econ_v1 to toggle on/off per-deployment.

Backfill and retro analysis: provide a migration job that synthesizes amortized per-token cost for historical requests using stored request-level metrics if event-level data missing. This job will live in Platform Data and be used for one-off analysis only.
data_schema_examples:
Example JSON event line (compact): {"ts":"2026-03-12T14:23:12.345Z","trace_id":"t_1a2b3c","emission_index":0,"token_index":7,"token_hash":"sha256:abcd...","latency_ms":2.7,"kv_status":"shadow_hit","kv_age_ms":120,"batch_id":3456,"model":"rwd-llama-13b-v2","instance":"g4dn.xlarge"}

ClickHouse table suggestions: table token_events (Date, Model String, BatchID UInt64, TraceID String, EmissionIndex UInt32, TokenIndex UInt32, TokenHash FixedString(32), LatencyMs Float32, KVStatus LowCardinality(String), KVAgeMs UInt32) TTL 90d on Date
